component: IMAP interface type and UIDNEXT migration phases

quotes.text: ImapUid can hold zero to indicate an invalid/missing UID.

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The original interface pass introduces ImapUid as an unsigned-long alias and keeps ImapUid_None equal to 0xffffffff for compatibility with message keys. It leaves signed UIDNEXT storage behind explicit casts. The typedef improves role names; it does not enforce a strong numeric type or complete UID/key separation. At the fixed accepted endpoint the type lives under base/public, zero means missing/invalid UID, the flag-state path rejects zero and UIDNEXT consumers are typed. These are later source phases. The first landing does not establish migrated databases, generated-binding compatibility or executed IMAP behavior.
title: The first ImapUid interface pass retains the old invalid-UID sentinel
